stories.title: Argentine Supreme Court sets limits on presidential use of emergency decrees
stories.summary: The judges declared a 2019 decree provision unconstitutional, ruling that the government failed to justify using emergency powers to amend a matter reserved for Congress La entrada Argentine Supreme Court sets limits on presidential use of emergency decrees se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald .
article_sentences: The Argentine Supreme Court of Justice declared an article of a 2019 presidential decree issued by then-President Mauricio Macri unconstitutional, in a decision that limits the president’s use of Necessity and Emergency Decrees (DNU, in Spanish).

The decision was reached unanimously by the three members who currently make up the Supreme Court — Horacio Rosatti, Carlos Rosenkrantz, and Ricardo Lorenzetti — on the grounds that the Executive Branch failed to demonstrate the existence of a situation of necessity and emergency that would justify amending by decree a matter under Congress’s jurisdiction.
Macri’s decree amended the Fair Trade regime, previously regulated by Law 22.802, to require intervention by the National Court of Appeals for Federal Civil and Commercial Matters.
However, after retail company Cencosud challenged a fine for mispricing, the court declared the requirement unconstitutional.
The case was then referred to the Federal Administrative Court, which also declined to hear it, ultimately sending the dispute to the Supreme Court.
In the Court’s view, regulation of the jurisdiction of federal courts is a matter that the National Constitution assigns “exclusively” to Congress.

According to the judges, the Executive Branch may exercise legislative authority through a decree “only under strictly exceptional circumstances and subject to formal requirements that constitute a limitation on — rather than an expansion of — its use.”

This occurs when one of two exceptional situations arises: either it is impossible to follow the ordinary legislative process because Congress cannot convene due to circumstances beyond its control, or there is such urgency that the matter must be resolved immediately, making it incompatible with the normal timeframe for enacting a law.
The judges found that neither situation could be demonstrated in this case.

“A reading of the grounds for the decree in question reveals not a single line dedicated to justifying the reasons or exceptional circumstances that led to the changes in the allocation of authority set forth therein,” the Court stated.

Although the decision did not overturn Macri’s emergency decree in its entirety — the declaration of unconstitutionality applied specifically to a single article — it sets a precedent that could affect current and future presidents by limiting their use of DNUs.

The ruling strengthens the authority of judges and lower courts to block or declare entire sections of emergency decrees unconstitutional, potentially affecting the government of Javier Milei, which has issued more than 80 such measures since taking office in December 2023.

stories.title: Russian movie Major Grom: The Game wins three awards at Chinese action film festival
stories.summary: The film won awards for Best Action Film, Best Action Screenplay and Best Editing
article_sentences: SHANGHAI, August 14.

Russian film Major Grom: The Game, based on comics from Russian publisher Bubble, won three awards at the 7th Jackie Chan International Action Film Week in China, the publisher’s Development Director Nina Potseluiko told TASS.
The Russian film was among the event’s major international winners.
"The film won awards for Best Action Film, Best Action Screenplay and Best Editing," she said.
Major Grom: The Game won three "Steel Man" awards.
Artem Gabrelyanov, Nikolay Shishkin and Ekaterina Krasner, the film’s screenwriters, won the award for Best Screenplay, while Dmitry Korabelnikov, the film’s editor, won the Best Editing award.
The 7th Jackie Chan International Action Film Week took place in Harbin from August 10 to 12.
The event brings together action-film creators from different countries and provides an international platform for professional exchange and promotion of the genre.
The film festival was founded by actor Jackie Chan and the organizing committee of the Shanghai International Film Festival.

stories.title: Syrian Air confirms resumption of direct air service between Damascus, Moscow
stories.summary: Direct flights between Damascus and Moscow were suspended in December 2024
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 14.
Syrian Air has confirmed that direct flights between Damascus and Moscow will be resumed this Sunday after a nearly 18-month break.

"The first direct flight in more than 1.5 years from Damascus to Moscow’s Sheremetyevo is scheduled for Sunday, August 16," an airline spokesman told TASS, adding that tickets for the Sunday flights are already on sale.
According to the spokesman, economy tickets are priced at around $491, while business class tickets will cost around $871.
The flight time will be four hours and 40 minutes.
Direct flights between Damascus and Moscow were suspended in December 2024 amid the turbulent situation in the Arab republic.
